title: The anti‑inflammatory activity of 2‑iminothiazolidines: the role of PPARgamma and M2 macrophage subpopulations.
authors: Mohr, Eduarda Talita Bramorski; Lubschinski, Taina Larissa; Moro, Pedro Augusto Marocco; Benvenutti, Larissa; Costa, Natali Tereza Capistrano; de Sousa, Pedro Luis Pereira Braga; Sa, Marcus Mandolesi; Hernandes, Marcelo Zaldini; Milton, Flora Aparecida; Santin, Jose Roberto; Dalmarco, Eduardo Monguilhott
one_liner_zh: 该文研究噻唑烷衍生物的抗炎活性及PPARγ/M2巨噬细胞极化作用，仅含分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Thiazolidine derivatives exert anti-inflammatory effects by inhibiting the NF-kappaB pathway and promoting macrophage polarization toward the anti-inflammatory M2 phenotype, partially through PPARgamma activation. Our previous work identified thiazolidine derivative 13 [methyl 2-(benzoylimino)-3-methyl-4-(4-nitrobenzyl)-1,3-thiazolidine-4-carboxylate] as a potent immunomodulator that reduces pro-inflammatory mediators and enhances anti-inflammatory markers. However, its direct interaction with PPARgamma remains unclear. This study aims to evaluate whether thiazolidine 13 activates PPARgamma and contributes to M2 macrophage polarization using LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 cells, cell transactivation assay and reporter gene (Hella cells), LPS-stimulated THP-1 cells, and molecular docking analysis. Compound 13 reduced NO(2)(-) production, CD80 expression, and pro-inflammatory cytokines while increasing IL-10, TGF-beta, and CD206 in LPS-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages. Compound 13 also inhibited NO production in LPS-stimulated THP-1 cells. These effects were only partially reversed by PPARgamma antagonists, suggesting additional PPARgamma-independent mechanisms, while the induction of CD206 was closely linked to partial PPARgamma activation. Docking studies supported this profile, showing that the (S) enantiomer of thiazolidine 13 adopts a binding mode typical of partial PPARgamma agonists and exhibits a higher predicted affinity than the (R) enantiomer. Compound 13 acts as a partial PPARgamma modulator capable of shifting macrophages from a pro-inflammatory toward an anti-inflammatory phenotype (M2-like). This dual action relies on the inhibition of NF-kappaB signaling and partial PPARgamma activation. The predominance of the M2-like subpopulation, underscores its role in resolving inflammation and promoting tissue repair.
abstract_zh: 噻唑烷衍生物通过抑制NF-kappaB通路并促进巨噬细胞向抗炎M2表型极化发挥抗炎作用，部分机制涉及PPARgamma激活。我们先前的研究鉴定出噻唑烷衍生物13 [2-(苯甲酰亚氨基)-3-甲基-4-(4-硝基苄基)-1,3-噻唑烷-4-羧酸甲酯] 作为一种强效免疫调节剂，可减少促炎介质并增强抗炎标志物。然而，其与PPARgamma的直接相互作用仍不清楚。本研究旨在利用LPS刺激的RAW 264.7细胞、细胞反式激活实验和报告基因（Hella细胞）、LPS刺激的THP-1细胞以及分子对接分析，评估噻唑烷13是否激活PPARgamma并促进M2巨噬细胞极化。化合物13在LPS刺激的RAW 264.7巨噬细胞中减少了NO₂⁻产生、CD80表达和促炎细胞因子，同时增加了IL-10、TGF-beta和CD206。化合物13还抑制了LPS刺激的THP-1细胞中NO的产生。这些效应仅被PPARgamma拮抗剂部分逆转，提示存在额外的PPARgamma非依赖机制，而CD206的诱导与部分PPARgamma激活密切相关。对接研究支持这一特征，显示噻唑烷13的(S)对映体采用典型的部分PPARgamma激动剂结合模式，并表现出比(R)对映体更高的预测亲和力。化合物13作为一种部分PPARgamma调节剂，能够将巨噬细胞从促炎表型转变为抗炎表型（M2样）。这种双重作用依赖于NF-kappaB信号传导的抑制和部分PPARgamma激活。M2样亚群的优势地位，凸显了其在解决炎症和促进组织修复中的作用。
